# Goban Studio v3.0.0

v3 is about how a game feels: an opponent that never freezes the window and
plays at a human pace, a teacher at your side when you want one, a review
you can play in, and a day that starts in one place.

## Download and first launch

| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | Ad-hoc signed, **not notarized**. Right-click the app → Open once. If macOS still blocks it: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Goban\ Studio.app` |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | **Not Authenticode-signed.** If SmartScreen appears, choose More info → Run anyway. WebView2 is preinstalled on Windows 10/11. |

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of all three files.

## Playing

- **No more frozen window.** KataGo now runs on its own thread and the page
  never waits on it; it keeps the position between moves instead of
  replaying the game each time.
- **A human pace.** Quick replies when the move is obvious, longer thought
  when it is not. Stronger levels resign a hopeless game; the gentlest
  levels play it out. When the board is settled, Goban Studio asks whether
  to count.
- **Clocks**: none, 30 seconds per move, or 10 minutes + 3 × 30 s byo-yomi.
- **Teaching mode** (on for newer players, off in Settings): before a move
  that loses a lot, it asks whether you want to think again — taking it back
  doesn't count as an undo — and it marks stones in atari. After the game,
  three takeaways: your biggest mistake, a good move, and what to practise.
- **A calmer panel**: the move list fills the space and folds away; captures
  count up with a small "+N"; an optional balance bar; two-click placement
  for trackpads; scoring, result and review follow on from each other.

## Reviewing

- **Play your own variations** on the review board, with live KataGo
  analysis of every position (win-rate numbers on the best candidates) and a
  territory estimate.
- **Mistakes explained**: what each key mistake cost and where — the group
  that died or the area that was lost is highlighted — and the kind of
  mistake it looks like (ladder, eye space, capturing race…).
- **Practise this**: one click turns a mistake into a drill that comes back
  on a spaced schedule.
- A larger balance chart with a board preview on hover.

## Your day

- **Today**: continue your game, today's five, the next lesson, a game
  suggested from your level and recent weak spots, your level over time.
- **A level that follows your results**: every rated game against the
  computer updates an estimate on the kyu/dan scale; opponents and handicap
  follow it unless you turn that off.
- **Today's five** now mixes your own mistakes, problems on your weakest
  theme, and spaced review.
- **Back and forward** (⌘[ / ⌘], mouse buttons) across places, lessons,
  problems and reviews; Esc always closes the top layer.

## Practice

- **254 problems** (up from 152), every one proved by the built-in solver, in
  22 themes — now with nets, snapbacks, throw-ins, connect-and-die, shortage
  of liberties and ko problems (a ko is accepted only where the problem says
  so). Difficulty spreads evenly across five measured grades. There are no
  seki problems yet.
- Lessons move on by themselves after a correct step; a wrong answer shows
  the refutation, then resets so you can try again.
- Problem windows are fitted tightly to the problem.

## Craft

- **Four board surfaces** (kaya, katsura, paper, slate), shell white stones
  and slate black stones, a high-contrast stone option, and real stone,
  capture and result sounds. All of it is generated by code in this
  repository; no third-party media.
- One motion system for every transition; reduced motion is respected,
  including on the board.
- A new icon family and app icon.
- A native menu bar on macOS (Game, View, Go, Help) in your language,
  alongside the standard Edit and Window menus.

## Quality

- Every pull request runs real-browser interface checks: the main flows,
  keyboard-only play, all four languages, performance budgets and visual
  comparison at three window sizes.
- Terminology across the four languages was reviewed against a written
  glossary (`docs/glossary.md`). It was a model review; native-speaker
  review is still recommended.
- A usability-test protocol is in `docs/usability.md`. The test with real
  people has **not** been run yet; the document says what was done instead.

## Known limits

- The macOS menu bar compiles and installs, but no automated test opens it;
  report anything odd there.
- Terminology was reviewed by a model against `docs/glossary.md`, not yet by
  native speakers.
- The usability test with real people has not been run (`docs/usability.md`).

## Your data

Everything from v2 carries over. New progress (rating, weak themes, your
mistake drills) starts with this version.
